title: Indonesia | OJK Consumer Protection under POJK 22/2023
tagline: Apply OJK's consumer protection rules at an Indonesian bank: fair products and sales, fair contracts and collection, complaints, secrecy and fraud awareness.
description:
This quest teaches the consumer protection rules that apply to conventional banks in Indonesia. It is based on **OJK Regulation (POJK) 22 of 2023 on consumer and public protection in the financial services sector**, issued by the Financial Services Authority (Otoritas Jasa Keuangan, OJK) under **Law 4 of 2023 on Financial Sector Development and Strengthening (the P2SK Law)**, together with **POJK 38 of 2025** on OJK lawsuits for consumers, the bank secrecy articles of the Banking Law as amended by the P2SK Law, and the consumer-facing parts of **POJK 12 of 2024** on anti-fraud strategy.

Article 91 of POJK 22/2023 requires banks to train staff on consumer protection: at least once a year for the consumer protection unit and at least once during employment for all other staff, covering complaint procedures, the unit's duties, product knowledge and ethical communication. This quest supports that duty for branch, sales, collections, complaint and operations staff and their managers.

In five stages you join a fictional Indonesian bank: principles and enforcement; product information, marketing and data; agreements and collection; complaints and disputes; and secrecy, fraud education and inspection readiness.

The quest builds knowledge and does not replace your bank's own consumer protection policies and procedures; always follow them and the latest OJK regulations.
audience: All employees of conventional commercial and rural banks in Indonesia who need consumer protection training at least once during employment
Consumer protection unit and complaint handling staff who must be trained every year
Branch, sales, telemarketing and bancassurance staff, including outsourced sales agents
Collections staff, collection agency managers and vendor managers
Compliance, operations and senior managers who oversee conduct and report to OJK
outcomes: Explain how the P2SK Law, POJK 22/2023 and POJK 38/2025 fit together and how OJK supervises and sanctions market conduct
Design, describe and market products within OJK's rules on information, suitability, consent, contact hours and data
Draft and change agreements fairly, honour cooling-off periods and collect debts within Articles 60 to 66
Handle complaints within the regulation's deadlines and guide customers to OJK, the LAPS body or the courts
Protect depositor secrecy, educate customers against fraud and meet the Article 91 training and OJK reporting duties

quest.name: The Fair Banking Mission
quest.premise: You have just joined Bank Arunika, a fictional conventional bank headquartered in Jakarta, as a consumer protection officer. A retired teacher in Yogyakarta has complained to OJK about an evening sales call, a product she did not understand, a branch that turned her son away and a collector who keeps phoning him. With Ratna, Bagus, Maria and Komang, clear five stages, then face the final boss: the examiner's exam.

badge.name: Fair Banking Guardian
badge.description: Awarded to bankers who can apply OJK's POJK 22/2023 consumer protection rules, from fair sales and collection to complaints, secrecy and fraud awareness.

cast.name: Ratna Wulandari
cast.role: Head of Consumer Protection Unit, Jakarta, your mentor

sessions.title: POJK 22/2023 and the P2SK Law: Principles, Duties and Enforcement
sessions.summary: Learn where Indonesia's consumer protection rules come from, who they bind, the seven principles, the basic conduct duties and how OJK supervises, sanctions and now sues under POJK 38/2025.
objectives: Explain how the P2SK Law and POJK 22/2023 fit together and which providers they cover
Apply the seven principles and the basic duties of good faith, non-discrimination and no dealings with unlicensed operators
Describe the bank's liability for staff and third parties and OJK's supervision and sanction tools
State what POJK 38/2025 changed in POJK 22/2023

cards.title: Day one at Bank Arunika
cards.setting: Consumer Protection Unit, Bank Arunika head office, Jakarta. Monday, 8:30 am.

lines.text: You have just joined Bank Arunika, a fictional conventional commercial bank with offices from Medan to Denpasar, as a consumer protection officer.
Welcome! I'm Ratna Wulandari, head of the Consumer Protection Unit. Your first file arrived this morning through OJK's consumer complaint system.
Ibu Siti Rahayu, a retired teacher in Yogyakarta. A telemarketer rang her at half past seven in the evening and she ended up with an insurance-linked savings plan she says she never understood.
Bagus Prasetyo, sales, Surabaya. That call came from our outsourced telesales vendor, not from our own staff. Surely the vendor answers for it?
Komang Adi Putra, branch manager in Denpasar. Worse: when her son phoned our Yogyakarta branch, someone told him complaints are only taken at head office.
Maria Simanjuntak, collections, Medan. And her credit card is overdue. Our collection agency has been ringing her son too.
One customer, five problems, one regulation: POJK 22/2023. Stage one is the Charter Hall. Learn who the rules cover and how OJK enforces them, then we open her file together.

scenes.heading: A stronger regulator
scenes.narration: In January 2023 Indonesia passed Law 4 of 2023 on Financial Sector Development and Strengthening, known as the P2SK Law. It gave the Financial Services Authority, OJK, an explicit role in protecting consumers and supervising market conduct.

scenes.heading: One rulebook
scenes.narration: OJK then issued POJK 22 of 2023 on consumer and public protection in the financial services sector. It was promulgated on 22 December 2023, took effect that day and replaced the earlier rule, POJK 6/POJK.07/2022.

scenes.heading: Who it covers
scenes.narration: It applies to every financial services business actor OJK licenses, called PUJK in Indonesian. Commercial banks and rural banks are on the list, alongside insurers, securities firms, finance companies and fintech lenders.

scenes.heading: What OJK watches
scenes.narration: Market conduct means how a provider designs products, provides and delivers information, markets, writes agreements, serves customers and handles complaints and disputes.

scenes.heading: Why you are here
scenes.narration: Article 91 requires every provider to train its staff on consumer protection: at least once a year for the consumer protection unit, and at least once during employment for everyone else.

cards.title: The seven consumer protection principles
cards.caption: Article 3 of POJK 22/2023 repeats the seven principles that Article 228 of the P2SK Law sets for the whole financial sector. Banks must apply them in every business activity.

items.label: 1. Adequate education
items.detail: Help people understand products, costs, risks and how to complain, from marketing to complaint handling.

items.label: 2. Transparent information
items.detail: Clear, accurate, honest, non-misleading information before, during and after use.

items.label: 3. Fair treatment
items.detail: Fair, non-discriminatory, responsible business; sales targets never outrank the customer's interest.

items.label: 4. Protection of assets and data
items.detail: Keep customers' assets, privacy and data safe and use them only as agreed and allowed by law.

items.label: 5. Effective complaints
items.detail: Simple, quick and affordable complaint handling and dispute resolution.

items.label: 6. Compliance enforcement
items.detail: The provider itself acts to make sure the rules are actually followed.

items.label: 7. Healthy competition
items.detail: Compete fairly; do not harm consumers to win market share.

cards.title: Principles in practice
cards.prompt: Match each principle with something a bank does to live it.

pairs.right: Running financial literacy activities and explaining risks before a sale
Giving a plain Bahasa Indonesia product summary before the customer decides
Keeping a salesperson away from handling a complaint about his own sale
Refusing to pass customer data to a partner without a lawful basis
Accepting complaints at every office, free of charge
Having a consumer protection unit that monitors and reports to the directors

cards.question: Which of these is NOT one of the seven consumer protection principles in POJK 22/2023?
options: Healthy competition
Enforcement of compliance
Guaranteed protection of investment returns
Adequate education
cards.explanation: The seven principles are adequate education, transparent information, fair treatment and responsible conduct, protection of assets, privacy and data, effective complaint handling and dispute resolution, compliance enforcement and healthy competition. Nothing in them guarantees investment returns.

cards.title: The basic conduct duties
cards.body:
Before any product rule applies, POJK 22/2023 sets **basic duties** for every provider:

- **Good faith** in all dealings, and **no discrimination**, including by third parties acting for the bank (Article 4).
- **No business with unlicensed operators.** A bank may not accept an application from, or partner with, an unlicensed financial business, must end any such partnership and must report a customer running one to OJK (Article 5).
- **Written policies and procedures** covering design, information, marketing, agreements, service and complaints, including equal access and special services for customers with disabilities and older customers (Article 8).
- A **code of ethics**, and controls that stop directors, staff and agents from enriching themselves or abusing their position to customers' cost (Article 9).
- **Liability for losses** caused by the errors, negligence or rule breaches of directors, commissioners, staff or third parties working for the bank, unless the bank proves the customer's own involvement or fault (Article 10).

cards.title: How OJK supervises market conduct
cards.caption: Articles 101 to 110 of POJK 22/2023. A thematic examination looks at products that may harm consumers; a special examination tests suspected violations.

items.label: Method
items.left: Analysis of reports and information, plus field observation

items.label: Trigger
items.left: Routine: complaints, reports, adverts, market signals
items.right: A theme OJK sets, or suspected breaches or consumer harm

items.label: Bank's duty
items.left: Supply documents and information by OJK's deadline
items.right: Show books, files, data and premises; never obstruct or influence examiners

items.label: Possible outcome
items.left: Orders to take or stop specific actions
items.right: Administrative sanctions and written orders, including to compensate consumers

cards.title: Required or not?
cards.prompt: Sort each statement about POJK 22/2023 duties for a commercial bank.

items.text: Written consumer protection policies covering product design to complaints
A consumer protection code of ethics set by the bank
Reporting to OJK a customer who runs an unlicensed financial business
Answering for losses caused by an outsourced agent's misconduct
Literacy activities at least once every semester
Ignoring the rules for products sold by a third-party vendor
Partnering with an unlicensed lender if the customer signs a waiver
Charging a fee to register a complaint

cards.title: Whose call was it?
cards.setting: Sales floor, Surabaya regional office. Video call with Jakarta.

lines.text: Our vendor's agent made that call, used his own script and earned his own commission. Why should Bank Arunika carry the blame?
Because Article 10 makes the bank liable for losses caused by staff and by third parties working for the bank. The vendor sold our product, under our name.
So the only escape is to prove Ibu Siti did something wrong herself?
That is the exception: the bank is not liable where it proves the customer's own involvement, error or breach. Otherwise we answer to her, and then we deal with the vendor.
And Article 4 says the bank must make sure third parties acting for it treat customers without discrimination too. Outsourcing the call does not outsource the duty.

cards.title: The partner nobody checked
cards.situation: A fast-growing digital lending company asks Bank Arunika to open a corporate account and sign a channeling partnership. Its pitch deck says it is 'licensing in progress'. A relationship manager wants to sign this week because the deal is large. The compliance check shows no OJK licence and no application on record.

choices.text: Sign now; the company says a licence is coming, so the risk is only on paper.
choices.outcome: Poor. Article 5 bars a bank from partnering with an unlicensed financial business. The exception covers parties that are genuinely in the licensing process with an authority; a claim in a pitch deck with nothing on record is not that.

choices.text: Decline the partnership, record the check, and escalate so the bank can consider reporting the company to OJK as an unlicensed operator.
choices.outcome: Best. The bank may not cooperate with an unlicensed operator, and where a customer or applicant runs unlicensed financial business, Article 5 requires a report to OJK's consumer protection function or regional office.

choices.text: Open the account but delay the partnership until the licence arrives.
choices.outcome: Partly right on the partnership, but the bank is also barred from approving product applications from unlicensed financial operators, so the account needs the same scrutiny and the report duty still applies.

cards.back: Written warning, restriction or freezing of products or business, removal of management, a fine, revocation of a product licence or revocation of the business licence.
Up to Rp15 billion under the regulation's standard sanction clause; heavier steps can come with or without a prior warning.
Direct supervision on a theme OJK chooses, looking at products or services that may cause consumer losses.
Direct supervision to prove suspected rule breaches or consumer losses by a specific provider.
OJK can order a provider to replace managers, stop or fix activities, return consumer assets, change contracts or compensate consumers.
A bank may object in writing, in Bahasa Indonesia, within 10 working days of the sanction letter; OJK decides within 10 working days.
OJK may announce administrative sanctions to the public, so a breach can become a reputational event.

cards.title: How the rulebook took shape
cards.caption: Dates as stated in the official texts published on ojk.go.id and by Bank Indonesia.

items.label: P2SK Law enacted
items.detail: Law 4/2023 sets seven principles and gives OJK market conduct powers.

items.label: POJK 22/2023 in force
items.detail: Replaces POJK 6/POJK.07/2022 on consumer protection.

items.label: POJK 12/2024 in force
items.detail: Integrated anti-fraud strategy, including yearly education.

items.label: Standard contracts deadline
items.detail: Older standard agreements had to be brought in line with POJK 22/2023.

items.label: POJK 38/2025 in force
items.detail: OJK lawsuits for consumers; revokes Articles 98(1)(b), 99 and 100 of POJK 22/2023.

cards.question: POJK 38/2025 changed POJK 22/2023 when it took effect on 22 December 2025. What did it do?
options: It revoked the whole of POJK 22/2023 and its training duty
It revoked the provisions on OJK lawsuits (Articles 98(1)(b), 99 and 100) and set new lawsuit rules
It removed OJK's power to order banks to resolve complaints
It moved complaint handling from banks to Bank Indonesia
cards.explanation: POJK 38/2025 sets detailed rules for lawsuits OJK files to protect consumers and revokes only Article 98(1)(b) and Articles 99 and 100 of POJK 22/2023. The rest of POJK 22/2023, including OJK's power to order a provider to resolve a complaint and the Article 91 training duty, still applies.

cards.title: Real case: OJK's market conduct enforcement in 2026
cards.body:
In its press release on the October 2026 Board of Commissioners meeting (SP 219/OJK/DKPU/XI/2026, 5 November 2026), OJK reported its consumer protection enforcement for the year:

- From 1 January to 15 October 2026: **150 written warnings to 98 providers**, **6 written instructions** and **51 fines to 44 providers**.
- **157 providers compensated consumers**, about **Rp84 billion** in total, from 1 January to 13 September 2026.
- From 1 January to 28 October 2026, market conduct supervision produced **77 written warnings and 44 fines of about Rp8.8 billion**, including for advert content, collection officers and transparency. OJK also ordered providers to change or stop non-compliant adverts and fix policies.
- Late or missing **self-assessment reports** for 2025 drew 8 fines (Rp570 million), and late **literacy and inclusion reports** drew 45 sanctions.

**Lesson:** enforcement is routine, it covers paperwork as well as conduct, and compensation is part of the outcome.

cards.title: Literacy and inclusion are duties too
cards.body:
Article 11 and 12 require each provider to run **financial literacy** and **financial inclusion** activities as an annual programme, **at least once every semester**, and to document them.

- Send the **plan report** for next year by **30 November**.
- Send **realisation reports** each semester, by **31 July** and **31 January**.
- Late reports draw daily fines; a commercial bank that fails to report faces a fine per report.

If your branch runs a school savings talk or a scam-awareness session, record it: it may count towards the programme.

cards.title: Charter Hall: what to remember
items: The P2SK Law (Law 4/2023) set seven consumer protection principles and gave OJK market conduct powers; POJK 22/2023 applies them to banks.
Basic duties: good faith, no discrimination, no business with unlicensed operators, written policies, a code of ethics.
The bank answers for losses caused by staff and third parties acting for it unless it proves the customer's own fault.
OJK supervises indirectly and through thematic and special examinations, and can sanction, order compensation and publish sanctions.
POJK 38/2025 now governs OJK lawsuits for consumers and revoked Articles 98(1)(b), 99 and 100 of POJK 22/2023.

cards.prompt: Think of one product your team sells through a third party, such as a vendor, agent or partner. If that party mistreated a customer tomorrow, how would Bank Arunika's liability under Article 10 play out, and what control would you want in place today?

quiz.question: Which law gave OJK its strengthened consumer protection and market conduct mandate that POJK 22/2023 implements?
options: Law 21 of 2011 on OJK in its original, unamended form
Law 4 of 2023 on Financial Sector Development and Strengthening (P2SK)
Bank Indonesia Regulation 3 of 2023
POJK 12 of 2024 on anti-fraud strategy
quiz.explanation: POJK 22/2023 opens by citing the P2SK Law, which strengthened OJK's consumer protection role and added market conduct supervision. BI Regulation 3/2023 governs consumer protection in activities Bank Indonesia supervises, not OJK's rulebook.

quiz.question: A rural bank (BPR) officer says POJK 22/2023 is only for commercial banks. What is correct?
options: It applies to rural banks only for their deposit products
Rural banks follow only Bank Indonesia's consumer rules
It applies to rural banks only from 2026
Rural banks are expressly listed among the providers the regulation covers
quiz.explanation: Article 2 lists commercial banks and rural banks (Bank Perekonomian Rakyat) among the financial services institutions bound by the regulation. The 2026 start date applies to cooperatives, not banks.

quiz.question: Bank Arunika's vendor mis-sells a product by phone and the customer loses money. Under Article 10, when can the bank avoid liability?
options: Whenever the misconduct was committed by an outside vendor's agent rather than by an employee on the bank's payroll
Only if it proves the customer's own involvement, error or breach caused the loss
Whenever the customer signed the application form
Only if OJK has not yet received a complaint
quiz.explanation: Article 10 makes the provider liable for losses from errors, negligence or rule breaches by directors, commissioners, staff or third parties working for it. The exception is where the provider proves the consumer's own involvement or fault. A signature alone does not prove that.

quiz.question: Which list correctly names administrative sanctions available under POJK 22/2023?
options: Written warning, product or business restriction or freeze, removal of management, fine, licence revocation
Written warning, imprisonment of directors, closure of all branches, public auction of assets
Verbal reminder, compulsory merger, customer refund levy, OJK management of the bank
Fine only, because warnings were abolished by the P2SK Law
quiz.explanation: The standard sanction clause lists a written warning, restriction or freezing of products, services or business, removal of management, an administrative fine, revocation of a product licence and revocation of the business licence. Criminal penalties come from laws, not from the POJK.

quiz.question: A team leader thinks OJK must always issue a written warning before any fine. What does POJK 22/2023 say?
options: Every fine must follow a written warning that the bank then failed to act on within the period set in the warning
Warnings are only used for rural banks
Fines require a court order first
Restrictions, fines and other heavier sanctions may be imposed with or without a prior written warning
quiz.explanation: The regulation states that sanctions from restriction to licence revocation may be imposed with or without first imposing a written warning. Planning on a 'first warning' is not a compliance strategy.

quiz.question: OJK opens a special examination of Bank Arunika's telesales. A manager suggests sending examiners only the cleaner call samples. What is the risk?
options: Obstructing an examination or influencing its results is prohibited and sanctionable
None, because the bank may choose which records to share
None, as long as all recordings are shared within a year
Only a reputational risk, since OJK cannot sanction obstruction
quiz.explanation: Article 108 requires the bank to show books, records, data and explanations within OJK's deadline and prohibits obstructing an examination or influencing examiners' findings. Breaches draw administrative sanctions and can lead to sanctions under the OJK Law as amended.

quiz.question: Bank Arunika receives a sanction letter it believes is wrong. What is the correct route?
options: File a civil lawsuit against OJK in the district court within 30 days, attaching the sanction letter and evidence
Ignore it until OJK publishes the sanction
File a written objection in Bahasa Indonesia with supporting evidence within 10 working days of the letter
Ask the LAPS financial services dispute body to review it
quiz.explanation: Article 115 lets a sanctioned provider object in writing within 10 working days of the sanction letter, with reasons and evidence. OJK grants, partly grants or rejects it within 10 working days, and payment of a fine is suspended while it decides.

quiz.question: Which statement about POJK 38/2025 is correct?
options: OJK lawsuits are class actions that need a power of attorney from each consumer
Consumers on OJK's lawsuit list bear no costs up to execution of the court decision
OJK sues only at a consumer's written request
It replaced POJK 22/2023 in full
quiz.explanation: POJK 38/2025 says OJK sues on legal standing given by law, not as a class action, based on its own assessment; consumers bear no costs, which come from OJK's budget. It revoked only Articles 98(1)(b), 99 and 100 of POJK 22/2023.

quiz.question: A customer who runs an unlicensed online lending business applies for a business account. What does Article 5 require?
options: Approve the application but monitor the account monthly and ask the customer to confirm in writing that a licence is pending
Approve it if the customer promises to apply for a licence
Do not approve the application, and report the customer's unlicensed activity to OJK
Report it only to the police, never to OJK
quiz.explanation: Article 5 bars approving product applications from unlicensed financial operators and requires the provider to report a consumer running unlicensed financial business to OJK's consumer protection function or a regional office. The exception covers parties genuinely in the licensing process.

quiz.question: By when must a bank send OJK its plan for next year's financial literacy and inclusion activities?
options: 31 January of the activity year
30 September of the activity year
30 November of the year before the activities
10 July of the year before
quiz.explanation: Article 14 sets 30 November before the activity year for the plan report. Realisation reports follow each semester by 31 July and 31 January. 30 September is the deadline for the annual self-assessment report.

sessions.title: Product Design, Information, Marketing and Customer Data
sessions.summary: Design products for a target market, give the right information at the right time, market within OJK's rules on consent, hours and suitability, and keep customer data within its limits.
objectives: Apply the design, testing and pricing duties to a new product
Deliver the general and personal product summaries and confirm understanding
Run telemarketing and adverts within Articles 35 to 40
Use customer data only within the confidentiality and consent rules

cards.title: The evening call
cards.setting: Telesales vendor floor used by Bank Arunika, Surabaya. Replaying a recorded call.

lines.text: You and Ratna listen to the recording of the call to Ibu Siti Rahayu. The time stamp reads 19:32 on a Tuesday.
(on the recording) Who is this? How did you get my number? I only have a savings account with you.
The vendor bought a list of pensioners from a data company. Conversion on that list was excellent, frankly.
The agent never said where her number came from, never checked she had agreed to marketing calls, and rang after six in the evening.
(on the recording) Is it a savings account? My granddaughter needs school fees in two years.
She told him her need and her horizon. He sold her a long-term insurance-linked plan anyway. Stage two is the Glass Counter: design, information, marketing and data.

cards.title: From drawing board to sales pitch

scenes.heading: Design for a target
scenes.narration: Article 25 says a product must be designed for a target group, weighing their needs and ability to pay against the product's features, risks and costs, and the design work must be documented.

scenes.heading: Test before launch
scenes.narration: Article 26 requires testing of new products to find risks that could harm consumers. If testing shows potential harm, the bank must review the product, and keep the test results.

scenes.heading: Price with a method
scenes.narration: Article 28 requires written guidelines for setting the price or fees of products and services.

scenes.heading: Speak plainly
scenes.narration: Article 29 requires information that is clear, accurate, honest, easy to access and not misleading, in simple Bahasa Indonesia, readable, with unfamiliar terms explained. Regional or foreign languages may be added, never substituted.

scenes.heading: Summarise
scenes.narration: Article 30 requires a product and service information summary covering the name and type, issuer, key features, benefits, risks, requirements, costs and, for products that collect, lend or manage funds, a simulation or performance data.

cards.title: The information journey for a new customer
cards.caption: Articles 32 to 34 of POJK 22/2023. Information given at marketing and before signing must also be documented.

items.label: 1. Marketing
items.detail: Information must be clear, honest and not misleading; offers name the bank and say it is licensed and supervised by OJK.

items.label: 2. Before deciding
items.detail: Give the general version of the product summary before the customer decides to use the product.

items.label: 3. Before signing
items.detail: Give the personal version, tailored to this customer, before the agreement is signed.

items.label: 4. Confirm understanding
items.detail: Confirm the customer understood the personal summary and keep evidence of it.

items.label: 5. Decision notice
items.detail: Tell the applicant whether the application is accepted, delayed or rejected, with reasons for a delay or rejection.

cards.title: Telesales call: allowed or not?
cards.prompt: Sort each practice for a marketing call to a customer's personal phone.

items.text: Calling on Saturday at 10:00 local time after the customer agreed to offers
Calling at 19:30 on a weekday without the customer asking for it
Opening with the bank's name and the purpose of the call
Telling the customer which company provided her number
Making consent to marketing calls a condition of opening a savings account
Recording the call and giving the customer access to it after she buys
Calling again next week after she withdrew her consent
Calling on a national holiday because she seemed interested

cards.question: Under Article 39, when may Bank Arunika make an offer through a customer's personal phone, absent the customer's own request or agreement to other times?
options: Any day, 07:00 to 21:00
Monday to Saturday, except national holidays, 08:00 to 18:00 local time
Monday to Friday only, 09:00 to 17:00 Jakarta time
Monday to Saturday, except national holidays, 08:00 to 20:00 local time
cards.explanation: Marketing through personal channels needs the consumer's prior consent and, unless the consumer agrees or asks otherwise, may only happen Monday to Saturday outside national holidays, 08:00 to 18:00 local time. The 08:00 to 20:00 window is the debt collection rule in Article 62.

cards.title: The product summary, two versions
cards.body:
Article 30 requires a **product and service information summary** in **two versions**:

- A **general version**, which must reach the prospect **before they decide** to use a product (Article 33(1)).
- A **personal version**, tailored to the individual, which must reach them **before the agreement is signed** (Article 33(2)).

The bank must **confirm the customer understood** the personal version and keep that confirmation in a document or other medium usable as evidence (Article 33(7) and (8)).

The summary may be delivered face to face or remotely, through print, electronic media or the customer's personal communication channels. For group products provided as an employee benefit, it can go to the employer.

Two exemptions: government or authority programmes, and products the customer uses repeatedly (Article 31).

Where a bank sells another provider's product under a **referral model**, each product owner is responsible for delivering and explaining its own summary (Article 33(6)).

cards.title: General versus personal summary
cards.caption: Both versions carry the same eight headings in Article 30(1); products that collect, lend or manage funds also need a simulation or historical performance.

items.label: When
items.left: Before the prospect decides to use the product

items.label: Content
items.left: Standard features, benefits, risks, costs, requirements
items.right: The same headings, tailored to this customer's figures

items.label: Extra duty
items.left: Available to anyone considering the product

items.label: Where the gap shows
items.left: Customer could not compare before choosing
items.right: Customer signed terms nobody checked she understood

cards.title: The poster in Denpasar
cards.setting: Bank Arunika branch, Denpasar. Komang shows a new promotional poster.

lines.text: Head office sent this loan poster. Big OJK logo in the corner, it makes customers feel safe.

That logo has to go. Article 35 says every offer, summary, promotion and advert must carry our name or logo and a statement that we are licensed and supervised by OJK, but the OJK logo itself is banned in that statement.
And the tiny line at the bottom that says 'terms apply'? Our customers in Ubud read English better than Indonesian.
The main text must be in simple Bahasa Indonesia, legible, with symbols and terms explained. You may add English or Balinese, but never instead of Bahasa Indonesia.

cards.title: The suitability shortcut
cards.situation: Ibu Siti told the agent she wanted savings for her granddaughter's school fees in two years and that she lives on a teacher's pension. The vendor's script had no suitability questions; it moved straight to a ten-year insurance-linked plan with charges taken from the cash value. Bagus asks you how to fix the process for next month's campaign.

choices.text: Add a disclaimer saying the customer is responsible for choosing the product.
choices.outcome: Poor. Article 37 puts the duty on the bank to consider whether the product fits the prospect's needs and ability, and a disclaimer that shifts responsibility to the consumer is the kind of clause Article 46 bans in standard agreements.

choices.text: Build a documented suitability step based on the bank's customer classification: background, job, finances and purpose. Stop the sale when the product does not fit.
choices.outcome: Best. Article 37 requires the bank to match products to the prospect's needs and ability using its own customer classification, considering background, occupation, finances and purpose, and to document the assessment.

choices.text: Keep the script but limit the campaign to customers under 60.
choices.outcome: Partly helpful, but an age filter is not a suitability assessment. Equal access must follow the bank's customer classification, and every sale still needs a documented needs-and-ability check.

cards.title: Marketing rules by article
cards.prompt: Match each POJK 22/2023 article to its marketing rule.

pairs.right: Name or logo and 'licensed and supervised by OJK', without the OJK logo
No exploiting people with no real choice; no selling unlicensed products
Assess and document fit with the prospect's needs and ability
Referral-model products: offer options from at least two providers, never force one
Personal-channel offers need consent, set hours, disclosure of data source
Disclose any conflict of interest when making an offer

cards.back: Keep consumers' data and information confidential and secure, applying the processing principles of the personal data protection law (Article 19).
Prohibited unless the bank has a lawful processing basis under data protection law; exchanges need written consent or a legal duty (Articles 20, 22, 23).
Do not use data of customers who ended their agreement, or of applicants who were rejected or withdrew, without a lawful basis (Article 22).
A bank may not require a prospect to agree to data sharing as a condition of getting a product (Article 22(2)).
Hold a written statement that the source obtained the person's consent, and tell the consumer where the data came from (Article 23(3)).
Give consumers access to a copy of their data and information as the law allows (Article 19(5)).

cards.question: A customer was rejected for a credit card in March. In June the cards team wants to use her application data for a personal-loan campaign. There is no other lawful processing basis. What does POJK 22/2023 say?
options: Allowed, because she once asked for a product
Allowed for six months after rejection
Not allowed: data of rejected applicants may not be used without a lawful basis
Allowed if the campaign is by email instead of phone
cards.explanation: Article 22 bars using data of prospects whose application was rejected or withdrawn, and of customers who have ended their agreement, unless the bank has a processing basis under personal data protection law (Article 23(1)). Channel and elapsed time make no difference.

cards.title: Real case: OJK orders on non-compliant adverts (2026)
cards.body:
OJK's November 2026 press release on its October Board meeting (SP 219/OJK/DKPU/XI/2026) reported that from 1 January to 28 October 2026 market conduct supervision led to **77 written warnings and 44 fines worth about Rp8.8 billion** for breaches of consumer protection rules. The breaches named include **information in advertisements**, collection officers and transparency.

OJK did not stop at fines. It also ordered providers to take **specific actions**: to **adjust or stop publishing adverts** that broke the rules, and to fix their policies and procedures based on supervisory findings.

**What this means at Bank Arunika:** every advert, brochure, social media post and poster is in scope. Check the bank's name or logo, the 'licensed and supervised by OJK' statement without the OJK logo, plain Bahasa Indonesia, and costs and risks shown as clearly as the benefits.

cards.title: Suitability notes that stand up
cards.body:
When OJK or a court looks at a sale, the question is whether the bank **considered** fit and **can prove it**.

- Record the customer's **stated need and time horizon** in their words.
- Note **income or pension, commitments and experience** with similar products.
- Explain why the product **fits** or why you offered an alternative.
- For long-term or complex products, note that the **cooling-off period** was explained.
- Disclose **commissions or conflicts** the customer should know about.

If the notes would not convince a stranger, the assessment did not happen.

cards.title: Glass Counter: what to remember
items: Design products for a defined target, test new products for consumer harm and keep the evidence.
Give the general summary before the decision and the personal summary before signing, then confirm and record understanding.
Offers carry the bank's name and 'licensed and supervised by OJK', never the OJK logo, in plain Bahasa Indonesia.
Personal-channel offers need prior consent, Monday to Saturday 08:00-18:00 local time, recorded, and stop when consent is withdrawn.
Assess and document suitability; never exploit customers with no real choice; disclose conflicts.
Customer data is confidential: no sharing, no use of rejected or former customers' data, without a lawful basis.

cards.prompt: Pick one marketing channel your branch or team uses: posters, WhatsApp, calls or social media. Which of the Articles 35 to 40 rules would an OJK examiner test first, and what evidence could you show today?

quiz.question: What must Article 25 product design consider?
options: The bank's sales targets for the year, the expected market share and the distribution channels already available
Only the product's expected profitability
The target consumers' needs and ability, and how features, risks and costs fit them
The preferences of the bank's largest customers
quiz.explanation: Article 25 requires design for target consumers, weighing their needs and ability and the fit of features, risks and costs, and requires the design work to be documented.

quiz.question: When must the personal version of the product summary reach the prospect?
options: After the first payment is made
Within 30 days of signing
Before the agreement is signed
Only if the customer asks for it
quiz.explanation: Article 33(2) requires the personal version before signing; the general version must come before the customer decides to use the product. Understanding of the personal version must then be confirmed and evidenced.

quiz.question: A brochure says 'Bank Arunika is licensed and supervised by OJK' next to the OJK logo. What is wrong?
options: Nothing, it meets Article 35
The statement should say 'guaranteed by OJK'
The OJK logo may not be used in that statement
Brochures need no such statement
quiz.explanation: Article 35 requires the provider's name or logo and a statement that it is licensed and supervised by OJK in offers, summaries, promotions and adverts, but forbids putting the OJK logo in that statement.

quiz.question: A vendor agent calls a customer at 18:45 on a Thursday. She had consented to offers but never asked for evening calls. Which rule is broken?
options: Article 39's personal-channel hours of 08:00 to 18:00 local time
Article 62's collection hours of 08:00 to 20:00
No rule, because she consented to offers
Article 51's cooling-off period
quiz.explanation: Consent to offers does not lift the time window. Unless the consumer agrees to or asks for other times, personal-channel offers may only be made Monday to Saturday outside national holidays, 08:00 to 18:00 local time.

quiz.question: Bank Arunika sells insurance from partner insurers under a referral model. What does Article 38 require?
options: Offer products from at least two providers and never force the customer to choose one
Offer the one partner insurer that pays the highest commission, as long as its product is explained clearly to the customer
Offer one partner's product, if the customer signs a waiver
Leave all explanation to the insurer's own staff
quiz.explanation: Unless sector rules say otherwise, a provider selling referral-model products must offer choices from at least two providers, may not force the customer to buy from one, and each product owner is responsible for its product.

quiz.question: The bank buys a list of phone numbers from a data company for a campaign. What must it have under Article 23?
options: A written statement that the source obtained the people's consent, and it must tell consumers the data source
Nothing beyond an invoice, provided the data company is a registered Indonesian business and the list is less than a year old
Only an invoice showing the data was paid for
OJK's prior approval of the list
quiz.explanation: When a provider obtains people's data from another party, it must hold a written statement that the other party obtained consent to share it, and must tell the consumer where the data came from; Article 39 repeats the source disclosure for calls.

quiz.question: A customer applies for a savings account. The form makes agreement to marketing calls and data sharing with partners compulsory. What is the problem?
options: Only the marketing consent is a problem
Only the data-sharing consent is a problem
Both consents may not be made a condition of using a product
There is no problem if the form is in Bahasa Indonesia
quiz.explanation: Article 39(2) bars requiring consent to personal-channel offers as a condition of using a product, and Article 22(2) bars requiring agreement to data sharing as a condition. Both clauses must be optional.

quiz.question: Which item is NOT on Article 30's list of contents for the product and service information summary?
options: Risks
The salesperson's personal sales target
Costs
Requirements and procedures
quiz.explanation: Article 30(1) lists name and type, issuer, main features, benefits, risks, requirements and procedures, costs and additional information, plus a simulation or performance data for products that collect, lend or manage funds. Personal targets are not product information.

quiz.question: A loan applicant is rejected. She asks why. What must the bank do under Article 34?
options: Tell her of the rejection and give the reason, unless another law says otherwise
Say nothing, because credit decisions and the scoring behind them are confidential internal information of the bank
Give reasons only if she complains to OJK
Give reasons only for rejections above a set amount
quiz.explanation: Article 34 requires the provider to inform applicants whether their application is accepted, delayed or rejected and, for a delay or rejection, to give the reason unless other laws provide otherwise.

quiz.question: A customer who agreed to phone offers by voice call later buys the product. What must the bank have done with the call?
options: Deleted it once the sale closed, keeping only the agent's written summary of what the customer agreed to
Kept only the agent's written notes
Recorded it only if the customer asked
Recorded it, kept the recording and given the customer access to it
quiz.explanation: Article 39 requires voice or video recording of offers made through personal channels, documentation of the recording when the consumer accepts, and access to the recording for a consumer who uses the product.

sessions.title: Agreements, Servicing and Fair Collection
sessions.summary: Write balanced agreements, change terms the right way, honour cooling-off, serve older and disabled customers well, and collect debts and repossess collateral within POJK 22/2023.
objectives: Spot banned exoneration clauses and meet the duties to explain and confirm before signing
Apply notice, consent and cooling-off rules to changes and complex products
Manage in-house and third-party collection within Articles 60 to 62
Follow the steps for repossessing and selling collateral

cards.title: Calls to the wrong person
cards.setting: Collections centre, Bank Arunika, Medan. Morning huddle.

lines.text: Ibu Siti's credit card is 40 days overdue. Our agency rang her four times yesterday, and twice they called her son's office in Semarang.
Her son is not the borrower. And four calls in a day is already 'continuous' contact.
The agency says it is licensed. But I have never seen certificates for its field staff.
(voice message) I want to pay. Nobody ever sent me a letter telling me how much I owe or what the late charges are.
Then stage three is the Recovery Road: fair agreements, fair changes, fair service and fair collection. We start with what she signed.

cards.title: What a fair agreement looks like

scenes.heading: Balance
scenes.narration: Article 44 requires agreements that are balanced, fair and reasonable, in writing, in Bahasa Indonesia, and never built on exploiting the consumer's situation.

scenes.heading: Say what it costs
scenes.narration: The agreement must state the costs the consumer pays and, where an agent or intermediary is paid commission out of the consumer's payments, that commission.

scenes.heading: Choose the forum
scenes.narration: It must record the agreed choice of dispute resolution, through the courts or outside them.

scenes.heading: Explain and confirm
scenes.narration: Article 45 requires the bank to explain costs, benefits, risks, rights and duties, give enough time to understand the clauses, and confirm understanding before signing, with evidence.

scenes.heading: No escape clauses
scenes.narration: Article 46 bans exoneration clauses in standard agreements, and Article 47 gives customers access to a copy they can obtain or print.

cards.title: Numbers that shape servicing and collection
cards.caption: All figures from POJK 22/2023 and its elucidation (Articles 49 to 51, 54, 62 and 117).

items.label: Notice of changes
items.detail: Minimum notice before a change to terms takes effect; for credit changes that add burdens, consent is sought too.

items.label: Cooling-off period
items.detail: Minimum for long-term or complex products, counted from the consumer's agreement.

items.label: Collection hours
items.detail: Local time, Monday to Saturday, outside national holidays, unless agreed with the consumer.

items.label: Calls a day
items.detail: The elucidation treats more than three contacts in one day as 'continuous' collection.

items.label: Older consumer
items.detail: Age from which the elucidation treats a person as an older consumer for special services.

items.label: Contract deadline
items.detail: Standard agreements made before POJK 22/2023 had to be adjusted by this date.

cards.title: Clause check
cards.prompt: Sort each clause in a standard credit card agreement.

items.text: The cardholder must pay the annual fee stated in the fee schedule
Disputes may be settled through the courts or the LAPS financial services body
The bank may change any rule at any time and the cardholder is bound once signed
The bank alone decides what any clause of this agreement means
The bank is not liable for mistakes by its staff or its collection agents
The cardholder waives the right to sue the bank over this agreement
The cardholder must give accurate information and use the card in good faith
The cardholder must prove any loss of service was not the bank's fault

cards.question: Bank Arunika sells a ten-year insurance-linked savings product through its branches. What does Article 51 require after the customer agrees?
options: A cooling-off period of at least 2 working days to reconsider, without penalty if she cancels
A cooling-off period of at least 14 calendar days
No cooling-off, because bank customers can always close accounts
A cooling-off period only if the customer is over 60
cards.explanation: Products that are long-term (over a year, per the elucidation) or complex need a cooling-off period of at least 2 working days from agreement, unless product-specific rules set their own. Cancelling in that period may not attract penalties.

cards.title: Changing the terms
cards.body:
Banks change products. POJK 22/2023 controls how.

**Any change affecting the agreement (Article 49):** inform the consumer **at least 30 working days** before it takes effect, unless a product rule sets another period. A consumer who disagrees may **end** the product. If the consumer stays silent after the notice period, the bank may treat it as agreement.

**Credit changes that add obligations or reduce rights (Article 50):** the bank must **notify**, **confirm the consumer's agreement or refusal**, and keep the confirmation as evidence, also **at least 30 working days** ahead. A consumer who refuses may end the product but must first settle what the agreement requires.

**Exceptions to the notice period:** changes set by the government or an authority, changes in a pricing reference already written into the agreement and set by an authority, and changes negotiated and put into an addendum.

The same applies to **transfer of receivables**: it must be in the credit agreement and notified to, or approved by, the consumer, without causing loss (Article 52).

cards.title: Your own collectors versus a collection agency
cards.caption: Article 61 of POJK 22/2023. Conduct rules in Article 62 apply to both.

items.label: Contract
items.right: Written agreement with sufficient stamp duty (bermeterai cukup)

items.label: Who qualifies
items.right: Licensed legal entity whose staff hold collection certification

items.label: Certification body
items.right: Professional certification body or association registered with OJK

items.label: Responsibility
items.right: Still the bank, for every impact of the arrangement

items.label: Oversight
items.right: Periodic evaluation of the partnership by the bank

cards.title: The agency file
cards.setting: Maria's office, Medan. Reviewing the agency contract.

lines.text: The agency is a limited company with a business licence. But only three of its twelve field staff have collection certificates.
Article 61 says a third-party collector must be a legal entity, licensed, and have staff certified in collection by a body registered with OJK. Nine uncertified collectors are working our accounts.
The agency also keeps a 'contact list' script: if the debtor doesn't answer, call relatives and the office.
Collection may only be aimed at the consumer, at the billing address or domicile, without threats, pressure or humiliation. Spreading her debt to her contacts is humiliation.

cards.title: Ninety days late
cards.situation: A borrower in Medan is 90 days overdue on a personal loan. He blocked the agency's number. The agency proposes: visit him on Sunday after church when he will surely be home, send a message to the WhatsApp group of his apartment block, and phone his employer's HR manager. Maria asks what to approve.

choices.text: Approve all three; he is clearly avoiding the debt.
choices.outcome: Poor. Sunday visits break the Monday-to-Saturday rule, posting to a group humiliates him and spreads his data, and calling the employer targets someone other than the consumer. The bank answers for all of it.

choices.text: Approve only the employer call, because HR can encourage him to pay.
choices.outcome: Still a breach. Article 62 bars collection aimed at anyone other than the consumer, and disclosing his debt to his employer harms him and his data rights.

choices.text: Reject all three. Send a warning letter with the required details and allow a weekday visit to his billing address, 08:00 to 20:00 local time, by certified staff.
choices.outcome: Best. Article 60 requires warning letters showing the due date, days late, outstanding principal, interest or margin and penalties. Article 62 limits collection to the consumer, at the billing address or domicile, Monday to Saturday outside holidays, 08:00 to 20:00, unless he agrees otherwise.

cards.title: Taking back collateral, step by step
cards.prompt: Put the steps for repossessing and selling collateral in the order POJK 22/2023 requires.
steps: Have an internal guideline on repossession that follows collateral law
Establish default: voluntary written handover, a court or LAPS decision, or another legal mechanism
Make sure the consumer received a warning letter and the bank holds the fiduciary, mortgage or hypothec certificate
Repossess under collateral law and record it in an official repossession report
Explain the outstanding principal, interest, penalties, repossession costs and the sale mechanism
Sell by public auction, or by private sale agreed with the consumer if that gets the best price
Explain the sale process and result, and return any surplus to the consumer

cards.back: Due date, number of days late, outstanding principal, the economic benefit of the financing (interest), and penalties or compensation owed (Article 60).
Only the consumer. Collection may not be directed at relatives, colleagues or other parties (Article 62).
At the billing address or domicile, Monday to Saturday outside national holidays, 08:00-20:00 local time, unless the consumer agrees otherwise.
Repossessing collateral in a public place, or spreading news of a late payment to the consumer's phone contacts (elucidation, Article 62).
No threats, violence, physical or verbal pressure, and no continuous, disturbing contact.
Allowed, but the bank stays responsible for all consequences and must evaluate the agency regularly (Article 61).

cards.question: A Bank Arunika collector visits a debtor's home at 19:30 on a Saturday. The debtor had not agreed to anything special. Is the timing allowed?
options: No, collection must end at 18:00
Yes, it is within Monday to Saturday, 08:00-20:00 local time, if it is not a national holiday
No, collection is only allowed on working days
Yes, collection may happen at any time once a warning letter was sent
cards.explanation: Article 62 allows collection Monday to Saturday, outside national holidays, from 08:00 to 20:00 local time. The 18:00 limit applies to marketing offers through personal channels, not to collection.

cards.title: Real case: OJK sanctions a lender over third-party collection (2026)
Serving older customers and customers with disabilities
cards.body:
Article 54 requires an information service, **equal access** for customers in the same classification, and support for **special services** for customers with disabilities and older customers (60 and over, per the elucidation).

The elucidation gives examples you can apply at a branch:

- **Braille** forms and accessible app features
- **Ramps** and **priority queues**
- **Trained staff** for customers with disabilities and older customers
- **Accessible ATMs** and information media

With someone like Ibu Siti, slow down, check understanding in your own words, and invite her to bring a trusted family member if she wishes.

cards.title: Recovery Road: what to remember
items: Agreements must be balanced, written, in Bahasa Indonesia, show costs and agent commissions, and record the chosen dispute forum.
Explain, allow time, and confirm understanding before signing; exoneration clauses in standard agreements are banned.
Give 30 working days' notice of changes; credit changes that add burdens need the consumer's confirmation too.
Long-term or complex products carry at least 2 working days' cooling-off with no penalty for cancelling.
Collect only from the consumer, at their address, Monday-Saturday 08:00-20:00, without threats or humiliation; agencies need certified staff and the bank stays liable.

cards.prompt: Look at one standard agreement or collection script you use. Which sentence would you rewrite first after this stage, and why?

quiz.question: Which clause is banned in a bank's standard agreement under Article 46?
options: The customer must pay the fees in the fee schedule
Disputes may go to court or to an out-of-court body
The bank may interpret the agreement's meaning on its own
The customer must give accurate information
quiz.explanation: Article 46 bans exoneration clauses, including one giving the provider sole power to interpret the agreement. Fee duties, dispute-forum choices and duties of accurate information are normal terms.

quiz.question: Bank Arunika plans to raise a credit card's annual fee. What notice does Article 49 require, absent a product-specific rule or an exception?
options: At least 30 working days before the change takes effect
At least 7 calendar days before the change
Notice within 30 days after the change
No notice if the fee is in the published tariff
quiz.explanation: Article 49 requires informing consumers at least 30 working days before a change affecting the agreement takes effect. A consumer who disagrees may end the product.

quiz.question: A bank changes a loan's terms so the borrower must provide extra collateral. What does Article 50 add beyond notice?
options: The bank must obtain OJK's prior approval of the new term before it can apply it to any existing borrower
The bank must confirm the borrower's agreement or refusal and keep evidence of it
Nothing, notice alone is enough
The bank must waive interest for a month
quiz.explanation: For credit changes that add obligations or reduce benefits or rights, the bank must notify, confirm acceptance or refusal, and record the confirmation, at least 30 working days ahead. A borrower who refuses may exit after settling obligations.

quiz.question: A customer cancels a long-term complex investment product on the first working day after signing. What may the bank NOT do?
options: Deduct costs that genuinely arose from using the product
Account for investment gains or losses she approved
Process the cancellation
Charge a penalty for cancelling within the cooling-off period
quiz.explanation: Article 51 forbids penalties or sanctions for cancelling during the cooling-off period. Where no product rule sets the refund, the bank returns at least what was paid, less costs incurred, plus or minus approved investment results.

quiz.question: Which conditions must a third-party collection agency meet under Article 61?
options: Registered with Bank Indonesia, insured against misconduct claims, and owned by an Indonesian citizen with banking experience
Any firm with experience, if the bank trains it
A partnership with OJK approval of each collector
Legal entity, licensed by the competent agency, staff certified in collection by a body registered with OJK
quiz.explanation: Article 61 requires a written stamped agreement, a legal-entity collector licensed by the competent agency, and staff certified in collection by a professional certification body or association registered with OJK. The bank stays responsible and must evaluate the arrangement periodically.

quiz.question: A collector calls a debtor five times in one afternoon. Which rule is engaged?
options: None, because all five calls were made within the permitted collection hours of 08:00 to 20:00 local time on a weekday
The 30 working day notice rule
The ban on continuous, disturbing collection; the elucidation treats more than three contacts a day as continuous
None, because the calls were to the consumer
quiz.explanation: Article 62 bars continuous collection that disturbs the consumer, and its elucidation defines continuous as more than three times in one day. Being within permitted hours does not cure it.

quiz.question: The bank wants to repossess a car under a fiduciary security. The borrower disputes the default and has not handed the car over. What must establish default?
options: The collector's own written assessment on site, countersigned by the branch manager and attached to the loan file
A court or LAPS decision, or another legal mechanism, since there is no voluntary written handover
A letter from the branch manager
Three missed payments alone
quiz.explanation: Article 64 requires proof of default through a written agreement with voluntary handover, a court or LAPS financial services decision, or another legal mechanism, plus a prior warning letter and a fiduciary, mortgage or hypothec certificate.

quiz.question: After an auction, collateral sells for more than the debt and costs. What must the bank do?
options: Return the surplus to the consumer within the agreed time, or as its internal guideline sets
Keep the surplus as a recovery fee to cover the bank's internal collection costs, which the agreement allows it to charge
Hold it until the consumer complains
Transfer it to OJK
quiz.explanation: Article 66 requires the provider to explain the sale process and result and return any excess to the consumer within the period agreed or, failing agreement, set in its internal guideline.

quiz.question: Which practice best meets Article 54 for an older customer who struggles with small print?
options: Asking her to come back with a lawyer
Refusing service until she brings a family member
Offering trained staff, priority service and information in an accessible format
Sending her to the mobile app
quiz.explanation: Article 54 requires an information service, equal access and support for special services for customers with disabilities and older customers; the elucidation lists trained staff, priority queues, ramps and accessible media.

quiz.question: A loan agreement allows the bank to sell the debt to another party. What does Article 52 require?
options: Only OJK must be notified in advance; the consumer is told after the transfer, through the new creditor's first statement
The transfer must be in the credit agreement, notified to or approved by the consumer, and cause no loss
Nothing, debts can always be sold freely
The consumer must pay a transfer fee
quiz.explanation: Article 52 requires transfers of receivables to follow the legal procedure, to be included in the credit agreement, to be notified to or approved by the consumer, and not to cause the consumer loss.

sessions.title: Complaints, the Consumer Protection Unit and Dispute Resolution
sessions.summary: Receive, acknowledge and resolve complaints on time, run the consumer protection unit with clear accountability, and guide unresolved cases to OJK, the LAPS body or the courts.
objectives: Handle oral and written complaints within the POJK 22/2023 deadlines
Explain the structure, staffing and tasks of the consumer protection function
Respond to complaints received through OJK's integrated system
Describe escalation routes, including OJK lawsuits under POJK 38/2025

cards.title: Turned away at the door
cards.setting: Bank Arunika branch, Yogyakarta. Ratna and Komang on a video call with the branch team.

lines.text: (OJK complaint text) My son went to the branch. A staff member said complaints are only handled at head office in Jakarta. Nobody gave him a number or a receipt.
I checked. The front desk thought only head office could log insurance-linked complaints.
Article 70 is plain: every office must accept complaints, oral or written, and record them. Article 67 says handling must be free.
Can my sales team just phone her and sort it out? They know the product best.
No. A salesperson involved in the complaint must not handle it. Stage four is the Hearing Room: the complaint clock, the unit that runs it, and where a dispute goes next.

scenes.heading: Receive
scenes.narration: Every office accepts complaints, oral or written, free of charge, and records each one. If the service runs 24 hours, complaint intake must too.

scenes.heading: Acknowledge
scenes.narration: An oral complaint gets a confirmation with a registration number and date. A written one gets a receipt with the number, date and a contact channel, issued by the consumer protection function.

scenes.heading: Resolve on time
scenes.narration: Oral complaints are settled within 5 working days. Written complaints are settled within 10 working days of complete documents, extendable once by 10 working days in set conditions, with written notice before the deadline.

scenes.heading: Respond
scenes.narration: The answer is either an explanation, where the bank did nothing wrong, or a settlement offer, where it did. The consumer gets reasonable time to accept or reject.

scenes.heading: Escalate
scenes.narration: If there is no agreement, the consumer can complain to OJK or take the dispute to the LAPS financial services alternative dispute resolution body or to court.

cards.title: The complaint clock
cards.caption: Articles 71 to 75 of POJK 22/2023. Working days, not calendar days.

items.label: Complaint received
items.detail: Record it; confirm an oral complaint or issue a written receipt.

items.label: Oral complaints
items.detail: Follow up and resolve, or ask for a written complaint with documents.

items.label: Missing documents
items.detail: Time the consumer gets to complete documents; extendable by 10 in set cases.

items.label: Written complaints
items.detail: Resolve from receipt of complete documents.

items.label: One extension
items.detail: In set conditions only, with written notice before the first deadline ends.

cards.title: Handling a written complaint
cards.prompt: Put the steps for a written complaint in the right order.
steps: Receive and record the complaint at any office, free of charge
Issue a receipt with registration number, date and contact channel
Ask for any missing documents and allow 10 working days to supply them
Investigate and resolve within 10 working days of complete documents
If set conditions apply, notify a 10 working day extension in writing before the deadline
Send a written response: an explanation or a settlement offer with time to decide
If there is no agreement, tell the consumer about OJK, the LAPS body and the courts

cards.question: A customer phones Bank Arunika's call centre to complain about a double debit. No documents are needed. By when must the bank resolve it?
options: Within 5 working days of receipt
Within 10 working days of receipt
Within 20 working days of receipt
Within 30 calendar days of receipt
cards.explanation: Article 74 requires oral complaints to be followed up and resolved within 5 working days. Where documents are needed and that is not possible, the bank asks the consumer to complain in writing, which starts the 10 working day clock once documents are complete.

cards.title: The consumer protection unit
cards.body:
Article 88 requires every provider to have a **function or unit** to implement consumer protection.

- It may be **combined** with another function, following sector rules, while **avoiding conflicts of interest**: the elucidation's example is a marketing employee who handles complaints and must not handle one he was involved in.
- Its size reflects **assets, offices, product complexity, customer classifications and staff numbers**.
- **Every office** must have the function for receiving, handling and resolving complaints, and the bank must **publicise** it.
- Complaint staff need **knowledge** of the bank's products and of complaint handling, and the **authority** to handle complaints.

Article 89 lists its tasks, including informing all staff about consumer protection, coordinating compliance and monitoring, **reporting to the directors** with recommendations, coordinating reports to OJK, handling complaints, preparing complaint material for the annual report and website, and acting as **liaison with OJK**.

cards.title: Who answers for consumer protection
cards.caption: Article 90 also requires a reporting mechanism for compliance with the regulation.

items.label: Board of Commissioners
items.detail: Oversees how the directors carry out their compliance responsibility (Article 90(2)).

items.label: Board of Directors
items.detail: Responsible for compliance with POJK 22/2023 (Article 90(1)).

items.label: Head office lead
items.detail: A director, or an officer one level below, appointed to run the function and reporting directly to the directors.

items.label: Office officers
items.detail: An officer or employee appointed at every office outside head office.

items.label: All staff
items.detail: Trained at least once during employment; the unit at least yearly (Article 91).

cards.title: Complaint vocabulary
cards.prompt: Match each term in POJK 22/2023 with its meaning.

pairs.right: Dissatisfaction from a real or potential loss because the bank did not honour the agreement
Information that the bank may have broken financial sector rules
The bank's explanation of the problem, or its final settlement offer
A disagreement that remains after the bank's own complaint process
The out-of-court body that resolves disputes between consumers and providers
OJK's system for receiving complaints, which banks must monitor

lines.text: My salesperson has a good relationship with Ibu Siti. Let him call and offer a refund of the first premium.
He sold her the product; he is part of what she is complaining about. The unit handles it, so there is no conflict of interest.
And OJK sent this complaint through its integrated system. Do we answer OJK or her?
Both, through the system. Article 96 says we must monitor complaints there, follow them up under Articles 70 to 78, and post our response there. She then has 10 working days to reply.

cards.title: The deadline is close
cards.situation: A written complaint about an unauthorised loan instalment arrived at the Denpasar branch with complete documents eight working days ago. The account was opened in Medan and the Medan branch has not answered Komang's emails. The 10 working day deadline ends in two days.

choices.text: Wait for Medan; the deadline is internal guidance anyway.
choices.outcome: Poor. The 10 working day limit is in Article 75, and missing it is sanctionable.

choices.text: Notify the customer in writing now of an extension of up to 10 working days, citing the different office and the communication delay, and escalate to Medan's leadership.
choices.outcome: Best. Article 75 allows one extension of up to 10 working days in set conditions, including where the receiving office differs from the office where the problem arose and there are communication obstacles, if the consumer is told in writing before the first deadline ends.

choices.text: Phone the customer to say there will be a delay.
choices.outcome: Partly right, but the extension must be notified in writing before the first deadline ends, and the reason must fall within the permitted conditions.

cards.title: May the bank decline to handle it?
cards.prompt: Article 76 lists when a bank may refuse to handle a complaint. Sort each case.

items.text: Consumer did not supply required documents within the set period
The same complaint was already resolved under the regulation
The matter is already in a civil court case
Complaint is about another bank's product with no tie to Bank Arunika
Consumer complained orally rather than in writing
Complaint was lodged at a branch, not head office
Complaint concerns a partner's product sold under a cooperation with the bank
Consumer is angry and uses harsh language

cards.back: Consumers may complain to OJK through its integrated consumer and public service system; banks must monitor it and respond there (Article 96).
The consumer has 10 working days to respond to the bank's answer; with no response, OJK marks the complaint as finished.
An OJK-approved alternative dispute resolution body for disputes after the bank's own process.
Consumers may go to court; in damages claims for unlawful acts, the bank bears the burden of proving it was not at fault (Article 82(4)).
OJK may sue on its own assessment; listed consumers can opt out in writing within 30 working days of the first announcement and pay no costs.
OJK's phone line and its consumer protection portal, which OJK cites as complaint channels.

cards.question: Ibu Siti's complaint arrives through OJK's integrated consumer service system. What must Bank Arunika do?
options: Wait for OJK to forward a formal letter before acting
Handle it under Articles 70 to 78 and submit its response through the system
Respond only to OJK, never to the consumer
Pass it to the LAPS body, since OJK is involved
cards.explanation: Article 96 requires providers to monitor complaints in OJK's system, follow them up under the bank's own complaint rules and deliver the response through the system. The consumer then has 10 working days to reply.

cards.title: Real case: OJK presses a bank to resolve customer fund losses (2026)
cards.body:
On 18 April 2026 OJK announced (SP 77/DKPU/OJK/IV/2026) that it had summoned the directors and management of **PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk** over a case of alleged misuse of customer funds at its **Aek Nabara sub-branch** in North Sumatra.

OJK asked BNI to:

- resolve the case **quickly, thoroughly and transparently**;
- **verify** customers' claims fully, **fulfil their rights**, and report progress to OJK regularly;
- carry out a full **internal investigation** of compliance, internal control and governance to find the root cause.

BNI had verified claims and **returned Rp7 billion** to customers by then, and had secured assets linked to the case with law enforcement. OJK said it would monitor the remaining funds and act if breaches were found.

**Link to the rules:** Article 10 makes a bank liable for losses caused by staff; Article 55 requires it to keep customers' funds safe.

cards.title: Reporting the complaint picture
cards.body:
Complaints also feed OJK reporting:

- A **complaint service report every semester**, due by the **10th of the month after** the semester ends (10 January and 10 July). Late reports draw daily fines; a commercial bank that fails to report is fined per report.
- The unit prepares **complaint material** for the annual report and website.
- Recurring themes go to the **directors** with recommendations.

Log the **channel, product, office, root cause and outcome** of every complaint. Good data turns complaints from a cost into an early warning.

cards.title: Hearing Room: what to remember
items: Every office accepts complaints, oral or written, free of charge, and records them.
Resolve oral complaints in 5 working days and written ones in 10 working days of complete documents, with one 10-day extension in set cases, notified in writing first.
A consumer protection function exists at every office, staffed by people with product knowledge and authority and free of conflicts.
Directors are responsible; commissioners oversee; a head office lead reports directly to the directors.
Unresolved cases go to OJK, the LAPS body or the courts; OJK may also sue under POJK 38/2025.

cards.prompt: If a customer walked into your office right now with a complaint about a product you did not sell, what would you say in the first two minutes, and what would you give them before they leave?

quiz.question: A branch tells a customer that complaints are only accepted at head office. Which rule does this break?
options: Complaints must be in writing
Every office must receive complaints submitted by consumers
Complaints must be filed with OJK first
None, if head office answers within 10 days
quiz.explanation: Article 70(3) requires every office of the provider to accept complaints, and Article 88(7) requires a complaint-handling function at every office.

quiz.question: What must a receipt for a written complaint contain at minimum?
options: Registration number, date received and a phone number or other contact channel
The customer's tax number and the product's interest rate
A signature from a director
The expected compensation amount
quiz.explanation: Article 73 requires a receipt with the registration number, date received and a phone number or other channel, signed or issued by staff of the consumer protection function.

quiz.question: A written complaint's documents became complete on Monday 3 March. Under Article 75, before any extension, by when must it be resolved?
options: Within 5 working days of 3 March
Within 20 working days of the first contact
Within 30 calendar days of 3 March
Within 10 working days of 3 March
quiz.explanation: The 10 working day clock for written complaints runs from receipt of complete documents. One extension of up to 10 working days is possible in set conditions, notified in writing before the first period ends.

quiz.question: Which situation allows the bank to extend the written complaint deadline under Article 75?
options: The complaint handler is on annual leave
The complaint needs special examination of the bank's documents
The bank wants to wait for a quieter month
The customer is a large depositor
quiz.explanation: Article 75(3) allows an extension where the receiving office differs from where the problem arose and there are communication obstacles, where special research into documents is needed, or other matters outside the provider's control.

quiz.question: A salesperson who handled a sale asks to manage the customer's complaint about that sale. What is the right response?
options: Allow it, since he knows the product best and the customer trusts him, provided his manager listens in to the call
Allow it if his manager supervises the call
Allow it if the customer agrees by phone
Refuse; the complaint goes to the consumer protection function to avoid a conflict of interest
quiz.explanation: Combined functions must avoid conflicts of interest; the elucidation gives the example of a marketing employee involved in a complaint who may not handle it. The fair-treatment principle makes the same point.

quiz.question: Who must the directors appoint to run the consumer protection function at head office?
options: A director, or an officer one level below the directors, reporting directly to the directors
Any branch employee with at least five years' service and product knowledge, reporting to the regional sales head
The internal auditor
An external consultant approved by OJK
quiz.explanation: Article 90(3) requires the directors to appoint a director or an officer one level below them at head office, and officers or staff at every other office. The head office lead reports directly to the directors.

quiz.question: A customer rejects Bank Arunika's oral response to her complaint. What must the bank do?
options: Confirm its position to her in writing
Close the file immediately
Refer her to the police
Offer double compensation automatically
quiz.explanation: Article 78(4) requires written confirmation where a consumer does not accept an oral complaint response. The bank should also tell her about OJK, the LAPS body and the courts.

quiz.question: How often must a bank report its complaint service to OJK, and by when?
options: Every quarter, by the end of the following month
Once a year, by 30 September
Only when OJK asks
Every semester, by the 10th of the month after the semester ends
