quiz.explanation: Article 79 requires a semester complaint service report by the 10th of the month after each semester. Quarterly reporting applied only until the first semester report under the new rule in July 2024.

quiz.question: In a court claim for damages based on an unlawful act, who must prove whether the bank was at fault?
options: The consumer
The bank
OJK
The LAPS body
quiz.explanation: Article 82(4) places the burden of proving the presence or absence of fault on the provider in damages claims based on unlawful acts.

quiz.question: OJK announces a lawsuit under POJK 38/2025 listing Bank Arunika's customers. A customer prefers to sue alone. What can she do?
options: Nothing; once listed, customers are bound by OJK's lawsuit and any later judgment, and cannot bring their own claims
Ask the bank to remove her from the list
Send OJK a written opt-out within 30 working days of the first announcement, then sue separately
Opt out at any time before judgment
quiz.explanation: POJK 38/2025 lets consumers who do not want to be included submit a written opt-out within 30 working days of the first announcement. Those who opt out may sue on their own but do not share in what OJK recovers.

sessions.title: Bank Secrecy, Anti-Fraud Education, Training and OJK Readiness
sessions.summary: Protect depositor secrecy under the Banking Law as amended by the P2SK Law, educate customers against fraud under POJK 12/2024, meet the Article 91 training duty and keep the evidence OJK expects.
objectives: Apply bank secrecy and its exceptions after the P2SK Law
Explain the anti-fraud education duties of POJK 12/2024 that protect consumers
Plan consumer protection training under Article 91 and the P2SK Law
Prepare the reports and evidence OJK reviews

cards.title: A call from someone in uniform

lines.text: A man phoned saying he is a police investigator. He wants Ibu Siti's son's balance and last month's transactions, today, by WhatsApp.
Did he send a written request with OJK's permission? Bank secrecy still applies after the P2SK Law, and criminal cases go through OJK.
No letter. Just a name and a badge number.
And this morning a customer in Medan lost Rp40 million to a fake 'bank officer' who asked for her one-time code.
Final stage: the Vault and the Review. Secrecy, anti-fraud education, training, and the evidence OJK expects. Then the final boss.

cards.title: Bank secrecy after the P2SK Law

scenes.heading: The core duty
scenes.narration: Article 14 of the P2SK Law rewrote the Banking Law's secrecy articles. Article 40 now says banks and affiliated parties must keep information about depositors and their deposits secret.

scenes.heading: Borrowers who also deposit
scenes.narration: If a customer is both a depositor and a borrower, the secrecy duty covers the information about them as a depositor.

scenes.heading: Listed exceptions
scenes.narration: Article 40A lists exceptions, such as civil cases involving the bank or customers, criminal cases, curators and liquidators, the customer's written request or consent, lawful heirs, tax, Bank Indonesia's and the deposit insurer's tasks, and reciprocal agreements between authorities.

scenes.heading: OJK permission
scenes.narration: Under Article 40B, OJK grants permission to open bank secrets for criminal cases and for mutual legal assistance, on a written request from the officials the law names.

scenes.heading: Personal risk
scenes.narration: Under amended Article 47, commissioners, directors, staff or affiliated parties who deliberately disclose protected information face prison of 2 to 4 years and a fine of Rp4 billion to Rp8 billion.

cards.title: Opening bank secrets: who and how
cards.caption: Articles 40A, 40B and 42 of the Banking Law as amended by Article 14 of the P2SK Law. Anyone who receives the information must keep it confidential (Article 40C).

items.label: Criminal case
items.left: Police, prosecutors, judges or other authorised investigators
items.right: Written request from the official named in the law, with OJK's written permission

items.label: Customer request
items.left: The depositor themself or someone they authorise
items.right: Written request, consent or power of attorney from the depositor

items.label: Tax
items.right: Request for financial information under tax law

items.label: Insolvency
items.right: Request based on the court's bankruptcy decision or appointment

cards.title: Disclose or refuse?
cards.prompt: Sort each request for a depositor's information.

items.text: Written request signed by the depositor for a balance letter to her embassy
Police request with OJK's written permission for a criminal investigation
Lawful heirs of a deceased depositor asking about his savings
Phone call from someone claiming to be a police officer, no letter
A depositor's husband asking for her balance without her consent
A journalist asking whether a celebrity banks with you
Curator appointed under a bankruptcy decision asking for the debtor's deposits
A collection agency asking for the borrower's savings balance

cards.question: A Bank Arunika teller deliberately tells a neighbour how much another customer has on deposit. What penalty does the amended Banking Law set for this?
options: Only an internal warning letter
Prison of 2 to 4 years and a fine of Rp4 billion to Rp8 billion
A fine of up to Rp15 billion on the bank only
Prison of up to 1 year, with no fine
cards.explanation: Amended Article 47(2) sets 2 to 4 years' imprisonment and a fine of Rp4 billion to Rp8 billion for commissioners, directors, staff or other affiliated parties who deliberately disclose information protected by Article 40. The Rp15 billion cap is the administrative fine in POJK 22/2023.

cards.title: Anti-fraud education that protects consumers
cards.body:
**POJK 12/2024** on anti-fraud strategy for financial services institutions took effect on **31 October 2024** and replaced the 2019 rule for commercial banks.

- The strategy must cover the parties involved in the business, at least **consumers**, **insiders** and **other parties**.
- It rests on **four pillars**: prevention; detection; investigation, reporting and sanctions; and monitoring, evaluation and follow-up (Article 5).
- **Article 7** requires **education and competence development for insiders** and **education or awareness for external parties** on the anti-fraud policy, **at least once a year**.
- The attachment's prevention pillar expects an **anti-fraud awareness programme for consumers**, for example brochures, banners, posters, contract clauses or written explanations.
- Fraud types include **extortion**, such as asking a debtor for money to ease a loan, and **leaking confidential information** about customers.

For consumers, this is the practical side of the data and asset protection principle in POJK 22/2023.

cards.title: The four anti-fraud pillars
cards.caption: Article 5 of POJK 12/2024. The cycle repeats as lessons from cases feed back into prevention.

items.label: Prevention
items.detail: Anti-fraud awareness for staff and consumers, vulnerability mapping, know-your-employee.

items.label: Detection
items.detail: Whistleblowing, surprise checks and surveillance systems.

items.label: Investigation, reporting, sanctions
items.detail: Investigate, report fraud to OJK and apply sanctions.

items.label: Monitoring and follow-up
items.detail: Evaluate cases and controls, then fix weaknesses.

lines.text: The customer says the caller knew her name and card number, so she trusted him and read out the code from her SMS.
Report it through the bank into the Indonesia Anti-Scam Centre right away. Speed is what lets funds be blocked.
She asks why we never warned her. Do we?
We should, at least yearly. POJK 12/2024 expects education for external parties, and the attachment names consumer awareness. Let's make our warnings impossible to miss.

cards.title: Scam victim at the counter
cards.situation: A customer arrives distressed: twenty minutes ago she transferred Rp25 million to an account a caller said was a 'safe account' after fake 'fraud alerts'. She asks for help and is embarrassed. The queue is long.

choices.text: Tell her the transfer was authorised, so nothing can be done, and suggest she go to the police.
choices.outcome: Poor. It ignores the speed that matters for blocking funds, the bank's complaint duties and its anti-fraud awareness role.

choices.text: Move her to priority service, log her report straight away through the bank's scam process so it reaches the Indonesia Anti-Scam Centre, register a complaint, and explain next steps calmly.
choices.outcome: Best. OJK reports that the Anti-Scam Centre receives victims' reports both through banks and directly, and blocks funds in reported accounts. Logging a complaint starts the bank's own clock under POJK 22/2023.

choices.text: Ask her to come back tomorrow with a written statement.
choices.outcome: Partly right on documentation, but delay lowers the chance of blocking funds. Take the report now and request documents afterwards.

cards.title: Real case: the Indonesia Anti-Scam Centre (2024-2026)
Training duties at a glance
cards.prompt: Match each training or education duty to its rule.

pairs.right: Consumer protection training at least once a year (POJK 22/2023, Art 91(3))
Consumer protection training at least once during employment (Art 91(4))

pairs.left: Front-line complaint staff in the unit
pairs.right: Complaint-service training before placement (elucidation, Art 91)
Complaint procedures, the unit's duties, product knowledge, ethics and communication
Anti-fraud education at least once a year (POJK 12/2024, Art 7)
Fund continuous staff education and training each year (P2SK Law, Art 252)

cards.title: Bank Arunika's consumer protection reporting year
cards.prompt: Put these OJK deadlines in calendar order, starting in January.
steps: 10 January: complaint service report for the second semester
31 January: literacy and inclusion realisation report for the second semester
10 July: complaint service report for the first semester
31 July: literacy and inclusion realisation report for the first semester
30 September: annual consumer protection self-assessment report
30 November: literacy and inclusion plan for the next year

cards.question: Bank Arunika's new IT engineer never deals with customers. What does Article 91 of POJK 22/2023 require for her?
options: Nothing, because she has no customer contact
Consumer protection training at least once a year
Consumer protection training at least once during her employment
Training only if she later moves to a branch
cards.explanation: Article 91 covers all employees. Staff of the consumer protection function or unit are trained at least yearly; everyone else at least once during their employment. The bank must also evaluate the training and improve it.

cards.title: Evidence an examiner will ask for
cards.body:
OJK can examine any part of consumer protection, so keep proof ready:

- **Training records** by employee, with dates, content and **evaluation results** (Article 91(6)-(7)).
- Product **design and testing** files and **suitability** assessments.
- **Product summaries**, understanding confirmations and **call recordings**.
- Complaint logs, receipts, deadlines met and responses.
- **Collection agency** contracts, certificates and evaluations.
- **Self-assessment** (by 30 September), complaint and literacy reports, and anti-fraud education for staff and customers.

If it is not documented, OJK will assume it did not happen.

cards.title: Vault and Review: what to remember
items: Depositor information stays secret under amended Banking Law Article 40, with listed exceptions; OJK permits openings for criminal cases.
Deliberate disclosure by staff can mean 2 to 4 years' prison and a Rp4-8 billion fine.
POJK 12/2024 requires yearly anti-fraud education for insiders and external parties, including consumer awareness.
Article 91: the consumer protection unit is trained yearly, all other staff at least once in their employment, with evaluation.
Keep the evidence: training, suitability, recordings, complaints, agency oversight and the reports OJK expects.

cards.prompt: Which customer at your office is most exposed to scams or mis-selling, and what one habit will you change to protect them, starting this week?

quiz.question: Under amended Banking Law Article 40, what must banks and affiliated parties keep secret?
options: Every fact about every borrower's loan
Information about depositors and their deposits
Only balances above Rp2 billion
Only information the customer marks as confidential
quiz.explanation: Article 40 as amended by the P2SK Law protects information about depositors and their deposits. Where a customer is both depositor and borrower, the information about them as a depositor is protected.

quiz.question: A police investigator needs a suspect's deposit details for a criminal case. What makes disclosure lawful?
options: A phone call from the investigator giving his name and badge number, followed by a confirmation message on WhatsApp
Approval from the branch manager
A written request from the official named in the law and OJK's written permission
An email from the suspect's employer
quiz.explanation: Articles 40B and 42 give OJK power to permit disclosure for criminal cases, on a written request from officials such as the police chief, attorney general or court chief. Anyone receiving the information must keep it confidential.

quiz.question: Which is NOT an exception to bank secrecy listed in amended Article 40A?
options: A written request or consent from the depositor
A request from a debt collection agency working for another lender
A request from the lawful heirs of a deceased depositor
A request for financial information for tax purposes
quiz.explanation: Article 40A lists court cases, curators and liquidators, written requests or consent from the depositor, lawful heirs, information exchange between banks, mutual legal assistance, tax, Bank Indonesia and deposit insurer tasks and reciprocal agreements. Collection agencies are not on the list.

quiz.question: How often does POJK 12/2024 require anti-fraud education for external parties such as customers?
options: Once every three years
Only after a fraud incident
Only for corporate customers
At least once a year
quiz.explanation: Article 7 requires education and competence development for insiders and education or awareness for external parties on the anti-fraud policy at least once a year.

quiz.question: A loan officer asks a borrower for 'an envelope' to speed up approval. How does POJK 12/2024 classify this?
options: A conflict of interest only
Misappropriation of inventory
Not fraud, if the loan is repaid
Extortion, a form of corruption
quiz.explanation: POJK 12/2024 lists extortion under corruption and gives the example of asking a consumer or debtor for money to ease a credit or service process.

quiz.question: Which are the four pillars of an anti-fraud strategy under POJK 12/2024?
options: Prevention; detection; investigation, reporting and sanctions; monitoring, evaluation and follow-up
Planning; selling; collecting; reporting, with a separate pillar for whistleblowing that sits outside the strategy
Identification; verification; screening; reporting
Governance; capital; liquidity; disclosure
quiz.explanation: Article 5 sets the four pillars. Consumer awareness programmes sit in the prevention pillar, whistleblowing in the detection pillar.

quiz.question: A customer loses money to a 'fake bank officer' scam and reports it at the branch within the hour. What is the best first action?
options: Tell her to wait 24 hours in case the money comes back on its own, then file a written complaint at her home branch
Close her account without explanation
Advise her to contact the scammer to negotiate
Log the report immediately through the bank's scam process to the Indonesia Anti-Scam Centre and record a complaint
quiz.explanation: OJK reports that the Anti-Scam Centre takes victims' reports lodged through banks and directly, and blocks funds in reported accounts. Fast logging improves the chance of blocking. Recording a complaint also starts the bank's POJK 22/2023 obligations.

quiz.question: By when must Bank Arunika send OJK its annual consumer protection self-assessment report?
options: 31 January each year
30 September each year
10 July each year
30 November each year
quiz.explanation: Article 85 requires the self-assessment report once a year, by 30 September. 30 November is the literacy and inclusion plan deadline.

quiz.question: What must the training under Article 91 of POJK 22/2023 cover?
options: Only the bank's sales targets, product pricing and cross-selling techniques, so that staff can serve customers efficiently
Only anti-money laundering rules
Only the history of OJK
Complaint procedures, the unit's main duties, product knowledge, and ethics and communication with consumers
quiz.explanation: Article 91(5) lists complaint service procedures, the duties of the consumer protection function, knowledge of the bank's products and services, and ethics and ways of communicating with consumers. The bank must evaluate the training and improve it.

quiz.question: Which statement about P2SK Law Article 252 is correct?
options: Financial sector actors must develop staff competence through continuous education and fund it each year
It sets a fixed number of training hours for every employee each year and requires OJK to approve each course in advance
It applies only to OJK staff
It requires training only for directors
quiz.explanation: Article 252 makes financial sector actors responsible for developing staff competence through continuous education and training and requires them to provide training funds from the current year's budget.

bank.question: Bank Arunika's head of retail says POJK 22/2023 covers only 'retail banking products'. Which description of market conduct supervision in the regulation is accurate?
options: Supervision of how a provider designs, informs, markets, contracts, serves and handles complaints and disputes
Supervision of capital adequacy, liquidity and credit quality ratios to keep each provider financially sound and stable over time
Supervision of the bank's financial statements only
Supervision of payment systems run by the central bank
bank.explanation: POJK 22/2023 defines market conduct supervision as supervision of provider behaviour in designing products, providing and delivering information, offering, drafting agreements, servicing and handling complaints and disputes. It contrasts this with prudential supervision of soundness.

bank.question: An outsourced agent of Bank Arunika refuses to serve a customer because of her ethnicity. The agent is not a bank employee. Which duty has the bank failed?
options: None, because POJK 22/2023 covers only the bank's own employees, and outside agents answer for themselves
Only a duty under labour law
The duty to run literacy programmes
To ensure third parties acting for it treat consumers without discrimination
bank.explanation: Article 4 requires non-discriminatory treatment and requires the provider to ensure that third parties working for or representing it also treat consumers without discrimination.

bank.question: A bank's compliance manual lists the consumer protection principles as 'education, transparency, fair treatment, data protection and complaints'. What is missing compared with POJK 22/2023 and the P2SK Law?
options: Profitability and growth
Capital adequacy and liquidity
Product innovation and speed to market
Compliance enforcement and healthy competition
bank.explanation: There are seven principles: adequate education; transparency; fair treatment and responsible conduct; protection of assets, privacy and data; effective complaint handling and dispute resolution; compliance enforcement; and healthy competition.

bank.question: The fair-treatment principle in the elucidation gives an example about sales targets. What does it say?
options: Sales targets must be approved by OJK every year and disclosed to customers in the product summary before they sign
Banks may not set sales targets at all
Targets are acceptable if commissions are disclosed
Marketing should focus on giving product details, not treat hitting sales targets as the main goal
bank.explanation: The elucidation of Article 3 explains fair treatment with the example that marketing should not make sales targets its main aim but should prioritise the product information given to consumers, and that complaint handling should not be done by staff linked to the complaint.

bank.question: OJK finds Bank Arunika in breach of Article 37 and imposes a fine and a deadline for remediation. The bank misses the deadline. What does the regulation provide?
options: The original fine is automatically cancelled
OJK must restart with a written warning
The bank can then face sanctions under the P2SK Law
The matter passes to Bank Indonesia
bank.explanation: Several articles, including Article 37, provide that if a provider fails to carry out an administrative sanction within the set period, it can be sanctioned under the law on financial sector development and strengthening.

bank.question: OJK requests documents from Bank Arunika as part of indirect supervision. The bank replies after OJK's deadline. Which statement is correct?
options: Indirect supervision requests are voluntary
Missing OJK's deadline for documents is itself a sanctionable breach
Only direct examinations carry deadlines
Late replies are fine if the documents are complete
bank.explanation: Article 104 lets OJK request documents and information in indirect supervision and requires the provider to comply within OJK's deadline, with administrative sanctions for breach.

bank.question: Which statement about OJK written orders under Article 110 of POJK 22/2023 is correct?
options: Written orders can only require a provider to stop or correct advertising; compensation must always go through the courts
Written orders need a court judgment first
OJK can order a provider to compensate consumers or return their assets
Written orders apply only to non-bank lenders
bank.explanation: Article 110 lets OJK issue written orders to replace managers, stop, limit or fix activities, return consumer assets, end or change harmful agreements, compensate consumers and other orders allowed by law.

bank.question: Under POJK 38/2025, which of these can OJK sue to recover consumer losses?
options: A provider whose licence was revoked and which is in liquidation
Only providers that currently hold a licence
Only parties that consumers name in a petition
Only parties already convicted of a crime
bank.explanation: POJK 38/2025 lets OJK sue providers that hold or have held an OJK licence, explained as those whose licences were revoked and are in liquidation, and other parties acting in bad faith. Liquidation does not stop OJK's lawsuit.

bank.question: A consumer reads that OJK will sue a failed investment firm and asks Bank Arunika how to add her name to OJK's list. What is accurate under POJK 38/2025?
options: She can join by paying the court fee
She can join any time before judgment
OJK does not accept requests to be added to the announced list
The bank can add her through its complaint system
bank.explanation: OJK announces a list of verified consumers before suing. It accepts written opt-outs within 30 working days of the first announcement but does not accept requests to be added to the list.

bank.question: A new 'flexi-saver' product passes legal review, but product testing shows older customers often misread its bonus conditions. What does Article 26 require?
options: Launch it and add a disclaimer
Review the product before launch and keep the test results
Launch it only to customers under 60
Report it to OJK and wait for approval
bank.explanation: Article 26 requires testing new products for risks of consumer harm, a review of the product where testing shows potential harm, and documentation of the results.

bank.question: Bank Arunika plans to send product summaries only in English to customers in Bali because many are expatriates. Which is correct?
options: English alone is acceptable for foreign customers, provided the bank keeps an Indonesian copy on file for OJK examiners
Bahasa Indonesia is needed only for loans
Documents must be in Bahasa Indonesia; English may be added as a supplement
Any language is fine if the customer signs a waiver
bank.explanation: Article 29 bans providing information or documents that do not use Bahasa Indonesia as the law requires, but allows regional or foreign languages in addition. Article 44 sets the same rule for agreements.

bank.question: Which product is exempt from the duty to provide the product and service information summary under Article 31?
options: A product the customer uses repeatedly
A credit card with a high limit
Any product sold online
Any product with fees below Rp1 million
bank.explanation: Article 31 exempts products and services that are government or authority programmes and those used repeatedly by the consumer.

bank.question: A relationship manager receives a higher commission from one partner insurer than another and recommends that insurer. What must the bank do under Article 40?
options: Nothing, because commissions are confidential business information that the bank may keep from customers
Disclose the conflict of interest to the customer when making the offer
Stop selling partner products altogether
Ask OJK for permission for each sale
bank.explanation: Article 40 requires a provider to tell prospects and customers about any conflict of interest when making an offer. Article 44 also requires agreements to show commissions paid to agents out of consumers' payments.

bank.question: A vendor calls a customer who agreed to offers. Which opening meets Article 39?
options: Starting the pitch at once to save her time, and explaining the bank's name and data source only if she asks for them
Saying the call is from OJK's partner programme
Asking for her PIN to verify her identity
Giving the bank's name, the purpose of the call and the source of her data if it came from another party
bank.explanation: Before offering a product through a personal channel, the provider must state its name and explain the purpose, and must say where it got the person's data if it came from another party.

bank.question: A small trader with no access to other credit, after a flood, is offered an emergency loan with very harsh terms because 'she has no other option'. Which rule is engaged most directly?
options: The ban on offering harmful products by exploiting a consumer who has no other choice
The cooling-off period rule, because emergency loans are complex products that need at least 2 working days to reconsider
The rule on product summaries for repeat customers
The collection hours rule
bank.explanation: Article 36 forbids offering products that harm or may harm prospects by exploiting the circumstances of people who have no other choice in making their decision.

bank.question: Under Article 54, what does 'equal access' mean according to the elucidation?
options: Every customer must be offered every product the bank sells, whatever their classification, income or stated purpose
All customers pay identical fees regardless of risk
Customers in the same classification get the same access to products and services
Branch hours must be the same everywhere
bank.explanation: Article 54(2) requires equal access according to the customer classification in Article 37, and the elucidation explains it as the same access for consumers with the same classification.

bank.question: Bank Arunika hands customer data to a vendor that runs its call centre. What does Article 19(4) require?
options: The vendor becomes solely responsible for the data once the outsourcing contract is signed and approved
The bank must first obtain OJK's approval
The bank must ensure the vendor keeps the data confidential and secure
Nothing, if the vendor is in Indonesia
bank.explanation: Where a provider works with another party to manage consumer data, it must make sure that party maintains confidentiality and security. The bank cannot pass the duty on.

bank.question: A customer withdraws her consent to marketing calls by email. The campaign team says the system update will take three months. What does Article 39(3) require?
options: The bank may continue until the system is updated
The bank may call once more to confirm her choice
Consent can only be withdrawn in person
The bank must stop offering products through her personal channels
bank.explanation: If a consumer withdraws consent to offers through personal channels, the provider must stop the offers. Article 23(4) allows withdrawal of data consent in writing or electronically.

bank.question: A standard loan contract states: 'The bank may change the rules after signing and the borrower agrees to be bound by any change.' What is the status of this clause?
options: Valid if printed in bold
Banned: it is an exoneration clause allowing one-sided changes
Valid if the borrower initials it
Valid for loans under one year
bank.explanation: Article 46 bans standard clauses letting the provider add, change or set further rules unilaterally after agreement, and clauses binding the consumer to such changes.

bank.question: A customer signs a five-year life-insurance-linked plan on Monday through the bank. On Tuesday the bank says a cooling-off period does not apply because a two-week reading period was given before signing. When could that argument be right?
options: Never; a cooling-off period always applies to every long-term bank product, whatever time was given before the customer signed
If the customer was genuinely given enough time, at least 2 working days, to study the clauses before signing
Always, once the customer signs
Only if the customer is under 60
bank.explanation: Article 51(7) exempts from the cooling-off duty products where the prospect was already given enough time under Article 45(2), of at least 2 working days. Government programmes, repeat use and group employee products are also exempt. Specific product rules for insurance may still apply.

bank.question: Bank Arunika's credit card terms let the bank raise the interest rate when a benchmark set by an authority changes, as written in the agreement. Does the 30 working day notice under Article 49 apply?
options: Yes, every interest rate change needs 30 working days' notice, even when it follows a benchmark already named in the agreement and set by an authority
No, changes in a pricing reference already set in the agreement and fixed by an authority are exempt from the notice period
Yes, and OJK must also approve it
No, card terms are never covered by POJK 22/2023
bank.explanation: Article 49(4) exempts from the notice period changes set by the government or an authority, changes in a pricing reference written into the agreement and set by an authority, and negotiated changes recorded in an addendum.

bank.question: A borrower refuses a credit change that adds an obligation and wants to end the loan. What does Article 50 say?
options: She may end it, but must first settle her obligations under the agreement
She may stop paying immediately
She must accept the change
The bank must waive the outstanding balance
bank.explanation: Article 50(4) and (5) let a consumer who rejects the change end the product, but she must first meet the obligations set in the agreement.

bank.question: Which warning letter meets Article 60?
options: One showing the due date, days late, outstanding principal, interest and any penalties
One showing only the total amount due, the payment deadline and a warning that the account will be passed to an agency
One threatening to tell the borrower's employer
One sent only after collateral is taken
bank.explanation: Article 60 requires warning letters, timed as the agreement sets, showing at least the due date, days late, outstanding principal, the economic benefit of the financing and penalties or compensation owed.

bank.question: Bank Arunika's collection agency contract has no stamp duty and the agency's staff certificates come from an unregistered training firm. Which two Article 61 conditions fail?
options: Bank Indonesia approval of the agency, and a minimum paid-up capital level set by OJK for collection companies
A court order, and an OJK licence for each collector
A written stamped agreement, and certification from a body registered with OJK
A deposit guarantee, and collectors on the bank's payroll
bank.explanation: Article 61 requires the partnership to be in a written agreement with sufficient stamp duty and collectors' staff to hold collection certification from a professional certification body or association registered with OJK. The agency must also be a licensed legal entity.

bank.question: A collector tows a borrower's car from a busy market car park in front of onlookers. The borrower is in default and agreed to hand over the car. Which rule is engaged?
options: None, because the borrower agreed in writing to hand over the car and the bank holds a valid fiduciary certificate for it
Only the collection hours rule
Only the warning letter rule
The ban on humiliating collection; the elucidation lists repossessing collateral in public
bank.explanation: Article 62 bars collection that humiliates the consumer, and its elucidation gives repossessing collateral in a public space as an example. Agreement to hand over does not permit a humiliating method.

bank.question: Before repossessing collateral, which documents must the bank hold under Article 64?
options: Only the original loan agreement, signed and stamped, together with the borrower's latest account statement
A police report and a court summons
OJK's written approval
Proof of default, a prior warning letter, and a fiduciary, mortgage or hypothec certificate
bank.explanation: Article 64 requires proven default, a warning letter to the consumer, and the bank's fiduciary, mortgage or hypothec certificate, with the repossession recorded in an official report.

bank.question: A customer complains orally about a disputed card transaction. The branch needs the merchant receipt, which she holds. What should happen?
options: Ask her to file a written complaint with the supporting documents
Close the complaint as incomplete
Resolve it within 5 working days without the receipt
Send her directly to OJK
bank.explanation: Article 74(2) says that where supporting documents are needed and the 5 working day oral deadline cannot be met, the provider asks the consumer to submit a written complaint with the documents.

bank.question: A customer's written complaint lacks a copy of her ID. The bank asks for it. She lives abroad and the copy is with her lawyer in Jakarta. What may the bank do?
options: Reject the complaint at once, because the documents were not attached when the complaint was first submitted to the branch
Give her unlimited time
Extend her time to supply documents by 10 working days, telling her before the first period ends
Ask OJK to decide
bank.explanation: Article 71 gives consumers 10 working days to complete documents, extendable by 10 working days where documents are not at the consumer's domicile or for other matters beyond her control. The extension must be communicated before the period ends.

bank.question: A complaint about a joint product needs input from a partner insurer. What does Article 75 require of the insurer?
options: Respond within 30 working days
Respond to the bank's request within 10 working days
Nothing, the bank alone is responsible
Respond only if OJK asks
bank.explanation: Where resolution depends on another party that is a provider, that party must deliver its follow-up within 10 working days of the receiving provider's request. Resolution beyond the normal time must be notified to the consumer in writing.

bank.question: A Bank Arunika call centre handles complaints by phone. What does Article 78 require about those calls?
options: Record only if the customer agrees to a settlement
Record the whole complaint process by voice or video
Recording is optional for complaints
Record only calls longer than five minutes
bank.explanation: Article 78(5) requires voice or video recording of the whole oral complaint process conducted through consumers' personal communication channels, done in line with the law.

bank.question: Bank Arunika decides to combine its consumer protection function with its compliance function. What must it ensure?
options: That OJK approves each combined role in advance and that the combined unit stops handling complaints from branches
That the function stops handling complaints
That combining follows sector rules and avoids conflicts of interest for staff
Nothing, combination is always prohibited
bank.explanation: Article 88 allows the function to be combined with another, following sector rules or, without them, as needed, while avoiding conflicts of interest for employees.

bank.question: Which is a task of the consumer protection function under Article 89?
options: Approving every loan application above the branch limit to make sure the product fits the customer's ability to pay
Setting the bank's sales targets
Auditing the financial statements
Acting as liaison with OJK and other authorities on consumer complaints
bank.explanation: Article 89 lists tasks including staff awareness, coordinating compliance, monitoring, reporting to directors, coordinating reports, handling complaints, preparing complaint material and acting as liaison with OJK and other authorities.

bank.question: Bank Arunika posts its response to a complaint in OJK's integrated system. The consumer does not respond. What happens?
options: The complaint stays open indefinitely until the consumer confirms in writing that she accepts the bank's response
After 10 working days without a response, OJK treats the complaint as finished
The bank must pay compensation
The complaint transfers to the LAPS body
bank.explanation: Article 96 gives the consumer 10 working days to respond to the provider's answer in OJK's system; if she does not, OJK deems the complaint finished.

bank.question: After the bank's process, a customer and Bank Arunika still disagree. Where can the customer take the dispute under Article 82?
options: Only to the bank's board of commissioners
Only to Bank Indonesia
Only to the police
To OJK's complaint service, an OJK-approved LAPS body, or the courts
bank.explanation: Article 82 lets the consumer complain to OJK within its authority or bring the dispute to an OJK-approved LAPS financial services body or to court. The bank may defend itself and present evidence.

bank.question: A bank employee shares a depositor's balance with a colleague at another bank as a 'favour'. Which statement is correct?
options: It is allowed because both employees work for banks and the inter-bank exchange of information is a listed exception
It is allowed if the amount is small
It is allowed if the depositor is a borrower too
Only information exchange between banks within the rules is an exception; a personal favour is not
bank.explanation: Article 40A allows exchange of information between banks as an exception, but that refers to the recognised inter-bank exchange, not an individual's private disclosure. Deliberate disclosure can trigger the criminal penalties in amended Article 47.

bank.question: Someone without OJK permission or legal authority forces a bank employee to reveal a depositor's data. What does amended Banking Law Article 47(1) set for the person who forced it?
options: A written warning to the person and an administrative fine on the bank of up to Rp15 billion under POJK 22/2023
A fine of up to Rp15 billion only
Prison of 2 to 4 years and a fine of Rp10 billion to Rp200 billion
No penalty, only the employee is liable
bank.explanation: Amended Article 47(1) punishes anyone who, without OJK permission or legal authority, deliberately forces a bank or affiliated party to disclose protected information with 2 to 4 years' prison and a fine of Rp10 billion to Rp200 billion.

bank.question: Who receiving depositor information under an Article 40A exception must keep it confidential?
options: Only bank employees
Every person who obtains it under the exception
Only OJK
No one, once it has been lawfully disclosed
bank.explanation: Article 40C requires anyone who obtains information about depositors and their deposits under the Article 40A exceptions to keep it confidential.

bank.question: The head of Bank Arunika's anti-fraud unit asks what POJK 12/2024 requires of her role. Which is correct?
options: The unit reports to a director and communicates directly with the Board of Commissioners; its head needs anti-fraud certification, experience or adequate sector experience
The unit reports to the sales director, who sets its annual targets, and its head needs no particular qualification
The unit must be outsourced
The head must be an OJK employee
bank.explanation: Article 8 requires a unit or function for the anti-fraud strategy, responsible to a director with direct communication and reporting to the Board of Commissioners, led by someone with anti-fraud certification, anti-fraud experience or adequate sector experience.

bank.question: Which activity would count towards POJK 12/2024's anti-fraud awareness for consumers?
options: Posters and written warnings explaining that bank staff never ask for one-time codes
An internal audit of head office cash handling, with findings reported to the Board of Commissioners at year end
A board meeting on fraud losses
A sales incentive for new accounts
bank.explanation: The attachment's prevention pillar expects the institution to raise consumers' fraud awareness through brochures, banners, posters, clauses, written explanations or other means.

bank.question: Bank Arunika trained all branch staff on consumer protection in 2023. In 2026 the consumer protection unit has not been retrained since. Which statement is correct?
options: Both groups are compliant, because the 2023 training satisfies a once-during-employment rule that applies to all staff
Branch staff may be compliant, but the unit should have been trained at least once a year
Both groups need yearly training
Only branch staff needed retraining
bank.explanation: Article 91 requires training at least once a year for the consumer protection function or unit and at least once during employment for other staff. The unit has missed its yearly training.

bank.question: After its Article 91 training, what else must Bank Arunika do?
options: Evaluate the process and impact of the training and improve materials and methods
Send each participant's test score to OJK within 30 days so that OJK can certify the training for the next year
Repeat the same course unchanged
Ask the LAPS body to certify it
bank.explanation: Article 91(6) and (7) require evaluation of the training's process and impact, for example staff understanding and fit of materials, and follow-up through better materials and methods.

bank.question: Bank Arunika misses the 30 September deadline for its self-assessment report. What does POJK 22/2023 provide?
options: Fines apply; after 30 days late it is treated as not submitted but must still be sent
Nothing happens until OJK's next examination, when the bank can explain the delay and submit the report then
The bank must wait until next year
Only a verbal reminder from OJK
bank.explanation: Articles 85 and 87 set fines for not submitting and daily fines for late submission. A report more than 30 days late is treated as not submitted, and the bank must still send it.
